bb.name: Contributor Dashboard
bb.description: A dashboard of how people contribute to one GitHub repository, from a local mirror of its pull requests, reviews, issues and releases. The page opens with an overview: a flow diagram of the delivery model's six stages, Identify to Learn, with a box for each step GitHub can see showing how many are waiting in it now and how long half take, and lines for where everything opened in the period went, thicker for more, including the paths a straight line hides: issues assigned without a plan, pull requests reviewed unasked, sent back with changes requested, merged with no review, or closed unmerged. Under it, an Issues section and a Pull requests section each time their steps with the median, p75 and p90, and clicking a step lists what is in it, every row naming whoever it is assigned to and offering to start a thread on it or copy its link. The Pull requests section also has PR Velocity, which opens with a chart of pull requests opened and merged each week, with bands showing the ones that bled into a later week and how many were still open, then charts for each person the pull requests they opened and the ones that merged, and Review Velocity, which opens with the same chart for review requests and the reviews that answered them, then the reviews requested of each person and the reviews they gave, over 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 3 months, or a range of dates you pick, drawn by day, week or month to suit the span, with the quietest people folded into rows of counts. Last, a Releases section draws the newest GitHub release in full: how many pull requests its notes list, how many are features, fixes, refactors, chores or dependency updates, which patch releases followed it, and how many each person merged and reviewed with their share of each, with the period's other releases as rows that open the same way and a See more button that adds earlier ones. Clicking a name opens that person's page, and clicking the Issues or Pull requests heading lists every one open now, oldest first.
